headline: A Thanksgiving Day storm brings 1–2 inches of rain (locally up to 3), wind gusts around 60 mph in New York City and Long Island (possibly 70 mph on Long Island), and widespread moderate coastal flooding at Thursday's high tides, with a Wind Advisory now covering most of the rest of the area.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Wednesday stays dry around New York City as high pressure passes to the north, with east-northeast winds of about 8–14 mph through the day. Clouds lower after about 1 AM Wednesday night in the city and along the south coast, and winds start to pick up toward Thursday morning.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: On Thanksgiving (Thursday) rain spreads in from the south during the morning and turns moderate to heavy in the afternoon and evening, with an isolated thunderstorm possible; the main storm window is roughly 10 AM through the overnight, though a surge of dry air from the south should cut the heavy rain and strongest winds short Thursday evening, leaving perhaps some light rain or drizzle. Expect 1–2 inches of rain, locally up to around 3 inches, with ponding on roads and widespread minor flooding in poor-drainage areas. A High Wind Watch remains for New York City, Long Island and nearby coastal northeast New Jersey from Thursday morning through late Thursday night for gusts around 60 mph (possibly 70 mph on Long Island if the stronger model scenario pans out), and a Wind Advisory covers Rockland, Westchester, much of northeast New Jersey and southern Connecticut from 10 AM Thursday to 5 AM Friday. On Friday the storm's cold core passes overhead with a few showers, perhaps a wet snowflake on the highest hills, and blustery west winds gusting about 29–40 mph.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Saturday stays breezy with west winds gusting about 23–35 mph and possibly some low clouds. Sunday turns quieter with light southwest winds of about 5–10 mph.

coast: With high tides after the recent full moon, minor coastal flooding is expected with Wednesday morning's high tide for southern Nassau County communities (Coastal Flood Advisory 5–11 AM Wednesday), with only localized minor flooding or none elsewhere. A Coastal Flood Watch covers the whole coastline except southeast Connecticut (which has a Coastal Flood Advisory from 7 AM Thursday to 3 PM Friday) from Thursday morning through Friday afternoon: gale- to storm-force east-northeast winds Thursday bring widespread moderate coastal flooding with both the Thursday morning and evening high tides, with possible major flooding along the western Great South Bay, significant impacts around Peconic Bay and along the western Long Island Sound shore, and minor to moderate flooding up the Hackensack, Hudson and Passaic rivers; heavy rain during Thursday evening's high tide could worsen coastal street flooding. Friday morning's high tide could bring another round of moderate flooding in the southern bays of Long Island and Queens, especially the eastern Great South Bay, but only minor flooding along Long Island Sound and New York Harbor as winds turn southwest. On the oceanfront, 8–12 foot breaking waves will cause widespread beach flooding and dune erosion with localized overwashes, and 3–6 foot waves along the western Sound and Twin Forks could cause dune erosion, splashover and isolated damage to shoreline and marina structures. For boaters, ocean waves stay around 5 feet overnight under a Small Craft Advisory, and one may be needed for all ocean waters Wednesday as seas build from the south; a Storm Watch covers all waters Thursday into Thursday night for gusts of 58 mph or more, with ocean seas near 20 feet and Sound waves near 10 feet in the late afternoon and evening. A southwest gale is possible Friday, especially on eastern waters, easing to small-craft conditions Saturday and possibly below that Sunday.
watch_for: Exact timing and strength of Thursday's peak winds — gusts could reach 70 mph on Long Island if the stronger scenario verifies.
Moderate to locally major coastal flooding at the Thursday morning and evening high tides, and again in the south shore bays Friday morning.
Street and poor-drainage flooding from heavy rain Thursday afternoon and evening, especially near the coast at high tide.
confidence: Forecasters are highly confident that strong winds and heavy rain will hit on Thanksgiving, but less certain about the exact timing and how strong gusts at ground level will get; Friday through Sunday look more settled.
